Folks —

I pulled the numbers into the sizing sheet. High-level technical read:

- Memory and long-context: The 32k contexts push us toward H100-class GPUs for the KV cache and activation memory headroom. H100 offers both higher HBM and faster NVLink/PCIe throughput which reduces paging for those 5% requests.

- Cost/perf mix: For the generation workload (avg 600 tokens), we can serve most traffic on L4 instances with slightly higher batching to hit p95 ~120-180ms depending on batching policy. Embeddings should be L4-first — much cheaper and meets the 80ms p95 with our optimized kernels.

- Fallback policy: Configure smart routing: primary route to L4 pool; when a request indicates long-context (>8192 tokens) route to H100 pool; if H100 saturated, fall back to A100 (as an intermediary) with an informative response header indicating longer processing window. A100 sits nicely as a generalist proc for medium long-contexts with lower per-hour cost than H100.

- Concurrency math (rough):
  * L4: ~70 concurrent gen streams per device for avg 600 tokens with dynamic batching (peak headroom -> 15 L4 GPUs covers peak with margins)
  * H100: ~8 concurrent long-context streams per device for 32k workloads (10 H100 GPUs covers long-context peak with ~60% utilization)
  * A100: reserve 5 A100 GPUs for spillover and for heavy-batch offline/ML retraining jobs.

- Ops notes: Ensure KV cache persistence per customer across nodes (to avoid re-warm) and set prefix caching for repeated prompts. Autoscale thresholds should prefer added L4 slots first to control cost; fail open to A100 only when H100 saturated.

I'll attach a quick cost sketch in the drive link and a sample routing policy.
